h: The Crown of Torah Gives Yisrael Holiness Forever

p: בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כד, א)
In the Midrash (this parsha, Vayikra Rabbah 24:1):
(תְּהִלִּים צב, ט) וְאַתָּה מָרוֹם לְעוֹלָם ה׳
"'And You, Hashem, are on high forever' (Tehillim 92:9)
You conduct Your world with exaltedness:
You gave the priesthood to Aharon forever, etc.;
You gave kingship to Dovid forever, etc.;
You gave holiness to Yisrael forever,
as it says, 'You shall be holy.'"
The matter follows what they said
of the Altar, of the Ark,
A crown indicates reaching up to the root:
that they are bound at the root
And likewise the word "on high" indicates
which with regard to Hashem Yisbarach
any perception or grasp there is in the world;
and this is "You conduct Your world with exaltedness."
means that it is for all eternity,
as they said in the Gemara:
"That of the Altar — Aharon merited it and took it;
that of the Table — Dovid merited it and took it"
and they merited it for all eternity;
"that of the Ark is still lying there;
And this is the crown of Torah,
at the time of Mattan Torah;
"For each and every one of Yisrael
and one corresponding to 'we will hear'";
and both are the crown of Torah:
"we will hear" is hearing the words of Torah,
the essence of the words of Torah is the deed,
(תְּהִלִּים קיא, י) וְשֵׂכֶל טוֹב לְכׇל עוֹשֵׂיהֶם
"'A good understanding to all who do them' (Tehillim 111:10)
it does not say 'to those who learn them'
(so is the reading of the Ein Yaakov,
וְכֵן הוּבָא בְּתוֹסָפוֹת סוֹטָה כב, ב)
and so it is cited in Tosafos, Sotah 22b);
and as they said in the Gemara (Yevamos 109b):
"'And you shall learn them and do them':
that one who occupies himself with Torah
and has no fear of Heaven
the words of Torah are called
"a price in the hand of a fool,"
and he is not wise at all.
are the tefillin of the hand
and the tefillin of the head:
are the crown of "we will hear";
and the tefillin of the hand,
which one prepares on account of the hands,
that everything be for His service,
this is the crown of "we will do."
וְאִיתָא (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, חֵלֶק ג קכג, רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב)
And it says (Raaya Mehemna, III 123b, top):
the vav is the Holy One, blessed be He
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
אֲנִי ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"I am Hashem Who dwells amid Bnei Yisrael";
the handiwork of the tzaddikim is called
And the Holy One, blessed be He,
and my portion is God forever"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב)
for so it says in the holy Zohar:
through which the work of the world is done"
and this is the Name of Lordship.
And throughout the work of Creation
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קנא, א)
"The Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah,
the tefillin of the head are the crown of "we will hear,"
the Holy One, blessed be He;
and those of the hand, "we will do,"
And at the time of Mattan Torah
each one of Yisrael was crowned
And although afterward they were removed,
and Moshe merited and took them (Shabbos there),
it says in the Pri Etz Chaim
that on Shabbos Moshe Rabbeinu returns
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Eruvin 96a):
that on Shabbos tefillin are not needed,
for they are themselves a sign;
that is, then Yisrael are crowned
with the crowns of "we will do and we will hear,"
and so all day and all night
בִּתְפִילִּין שֶׁל רֹאשׁ וּתְפִילִּין שֶׁל יָד
with the tefillin of the head and the tefillin of the hand.
And this is what it says:
for this is the crown of Torah,
which Yisrael merited for all eternity.

p: "In this world you are called holy;
and whoever is left in Yerushalayim
And the end of the pasuk is:
and this is the World to Come;
as we find in the Gemara
that one who denies the Resurrection of the Dead
has no portion in the World to Come:
"he denied the Resurrection of the Dead, etc.";
the Resurrection of the Dead and the World to Come are one.
have a portion in the World to Come,"
and all Yisrael will be holy;
and this is what it says:
And it appears that the Midrashim also inferred this
from the wording of the verse, "You shall be holy,"
which is the language of promise,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג פא, א)
וְכֵן יֵשׁ עוֹד הַבְטָחָה בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ
And so there is another promise in this parsha:
"And you shall be holy to Me, etc.,
and I have separated you, etc."
that Hashem Yisbarach will give holiness to Yisrael.
And the opening of the Midrash Rabbah
"And Hashem of Hosts is exalted through justice":
אֵימָתַי שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
"When is the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He,
When He carries out the attribute of judgment, etc."
And what connection does this have
But the intent is the end of the exposition,
"And I will magnify Myself and sanctify Myself,
and I will be known in the eyes of many nations";
the perception and grasp of this world
and it writes "and I will be known, etc.";
that is, that the holiness is forever.
And this is the meaning of the word
"To know that I am Hashem Who sanctifies you";
and Shabbos is its name, etc."
הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
is the attribute of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"And they will sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov";
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him
And the Ramban, of blessed memory, writes
that the mitzvah "You shall be holy"
is a positive commandment for every Jew:
sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you;
that is, that he not feel his own pleasure,
for that is the venom of the serpent;
as we find with Yishai, the father of Dovid,
of whom the verse is explained:
that he died through the venom of the serpent
And we find in Midrash Rabbah
(beginning of Tazria, according to the reading of the Yalkut):
the most pious of the pious,
it is impossible that there not be in him
that is, even though he did not commit
any prohibition in all his days,
only that he felt his own pleasure,
which is the venom of the serpent,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה כׇּל אֶחָד מִזַּרְעָם
and through this each of their descendants
וְעַל זֶה בָּא מִצְוַת קְדוֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ
And for this came the mitzvah "You shall be holy":
sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you,
to bring holiness into optional matters;
וּכְבָר הִקְשׁוּ בְּתוֹסָפוֹת (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יא, א)
that "there never ceased from their table, etc."
that he was like Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
who did not feel any pleasure,
and all his pleasures were in holiness,
like Adam HaRishon before the sin.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ לֹא מֵת
And therefore "Yaakov Avinu did not die"
would come every Shabbos eve to his home
and it says in Sefer Chassidim (siman 1129)
that he exempted the public with Kiddush
who are free from the mitzvos,
for his status was that of a living person
who had not died at all.
And it is brought from Rabbi Nosson Shapira:
"he is a spark of Yaakov Avinu."
And whoever is of the seed of Yaakov
in this world and in the World to Come;
have a portion in the World to Come,"
And this is the meaning of the wording of the blessing
that the Geonim, of blessed memory, instituted
"Who sanctified the fetus in its mother's womb";
וְהִקְשָׁה עַל זֶה הָרֹא״שׁ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
and the Rosh, of blessed memory, asked on this
if it refers to the holiness of the firstborn,
the Torah made it depend on the opening of the womb.
But according to what was said,
it refers to every Jewish fetus,
שֶׁזֶּהוּ חֵלֶק יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
for this is the portion of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
so that since one is of his seed,
there is still the evil inclination,
so that he feels his own pleasure;
where he has no evil inclination
and this is what they said in the Gemara (Niddah 30b):
"And a lamp is lit for him above his head"
the crown of "we will do and we will hear,"
And then, in the mother's womb, they are
when the evil inclination was uprooted from their heart

p: And the opening of Midrash Tanchuma
"And Hashem of Hosts is exalted through justice":
"When does the Holy One, blessed be He, become
When He executes judgment upon the wicked,
And this is as we said
with regard to the Holy One, blessed be He,
that is, in the first attribute,
of the emanation of the attributes),
which is the attribute of Kesser,
above the perception and grasp of this world.
of the matter of the future,
that was given over to the burning fire"
that is, when the wicked are cut off
And it is hard before Hashem Yisbarach
with his hands on his loins, etc.?"
He to Whom all strength belongs.
What is 'And all faces have turned pale'?
the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them:
"My handiwork is drowning in the sea, etc."
And as for Rav using the expression
it is because what makes it hard before Him to destroy them
and throughout the work of Creation
And this is what he said:
and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, is pained
And only when He returns the world
to the beginning of the Thought,
which they expounded as "for the sake of Yisrael,
that is, He returns the world
to the beginnings of the emanation of the attributes,
which is the beginning of the Thought;
and he reached the Ancient of Days, etc.";
for immediately upon the destruction of the wicked
the spirit of Mashiach is aroused to come.
"And the earth was formless and void, and darkness"
for this is the spirit of Mashiach.
And afterward it says in Midrash Tanchuma:
And what is 'and the Ancient of Days sat,' etc.?"
that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits among them
like the head of the court
וְהִיא עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
And this is along the lines of what they said in the Midrash
"'Your throne is established from of old;
but from when You stood at the Sea
a parable to a king, etc."
And this was at the Splitting of the Sea,
when there was the revelation of Atika
that He executes upon the nations of the world,
for it is hard to destroy them;
and this is why the Midrash cites
that is, before He judges them;
(which is the end of the pasuk 'And He is exalted, etc.')
He is sanctified in His world
בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה צְדָקָה עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳
when He does righteousness with Yisrael, etc.;
and you are sanctified through Me
and I am sanctified through you,
as it says, 'And you shall be holy, etc.'"
judgment is carried out upon the nations of the world
when the light of Mashiach begins to hover,
for "he reached the Ancient of Days,"
that was created on the first day
and hidden away for the tzaddikim for the future;
corresponding to the five books of the Torah.
And it says in the holy Zohar,
and the revelation of the light
which is holiness, as was said.
And likewise at this meal of Atika
we say: "His light will rest upon it"
the light hidden away for the future,
which is the light of Atika,
from the tip of the upper yud,
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג י, ב; סה, ב)
which is the revelation of secrets
that there is no power in this world to attain;
that the Sages called the good of the World to Come
And although the Raavad, of blessed memory, disputed him
and wrote that "silence would have been better for him,"
the words of the Rambam, of blessed memory,
are explicit in the holy Zohar
that were not revealed to man
since the day the world was created,
and are destined to be revealed
to the tzaddikim in the future"
"All the Torah that a person learns
before the Torah of the World to Come";
in which the soul will rejoice:
(יְשַׁעְיָה לה, י) שִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם עַל רֹאשָׁם
And it says in the Gemara (Shabbos 88a)
that the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future
"the joy of old upon their heads."
And this is what it says in the holy Zohar:
that is, the crowns of "we will do and we will hear"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רטו, א)
that is, secrets from the dew of Atika,
with all precious and pleasant wealth";
(אִיּוֹב כח, י) כׇּל יְקָר רָאֲתָה עֵינוֹ
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues:
things that were not revealed to Moshe
were revealed to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues"
And this is what we say:
which is revealed to baalei teshuvah;
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה חֲדוּ חַצְדֵי חַקְלָא
and through this "the reapers of the field rejoice,"
who are the members of the Idra,
who entered the chambers of the Chariot,
